EBITDA $1-2m, all company guidance in the Q2 release of 2026-08-06 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm). Street revenue consensus is $43.5m (Benzinga https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CHGG/earnings-forecasts) and $43.52m (MarketBeat/TheStockObserver), so two estimate sources agree with the guide midpoint. EPS consensus disagrees: -$0.07 vs -$0.09, from one analyst on Yahoo. Q4 2026 consensus could not be sourced, and that is the line the stock usually trades on.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: MarketBeat page read 2026-11-02 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/CHGG/short-interest/): 5.57% of float short, 9.14 days to cover, recently down 0.68%. Curved Trading/FINRA via search snippet: about 6.0m shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement, down from 6.3m at 09-15, DTC 9.4. Moderate short interest, but high days to cover on thin $0.47m/day turnover, so some squeeze risk on a positive surprise; not a crowded short at 18-23%. No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided, put/call OI ratio 0.18 on 684 contracts total), so there is no skew statement. Run-up is -1.8% over 5 and 20 days; the stock is -54% from its 52-week high and +57% off its low; spot $0.707.

evidence.text: Chegg has beaten its own guide by wide margins two quarters running: Q2 2026 revenue $51.8m against a $49-50m guide and adj. EBITDA $9.1m against $5-6m; Q1 2026 revenue $63.3m against a $60-62m guide and EBITDA $15.5m against $11-12m. Repeating the Q2 pattern (+4.6% over midpoint) on the Q3 guide of $43-44m and $1-2m EBITDA points to roughly $45m revenue (+3% against the $43.5m consensus) and EBITDA of $3-5m against $1.5m. The consensus sits exactly on the guide midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q2 2026 (2026-08-06) beat revenue and EBITDA and the stock fell 14.56% close to close on a weak Q3 guide. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06) beat by 3.7% on revenue and traded down 11.6% intraday on a weak Q2 guide, though the baseline closes it +10.34%. Q4 2025 (2026-02-09) closed -10.67%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $43.5m equals the guide midpoint, so the street has not modelled the habitual beat. If the beat were priced, revenue consensus would sit around $45m and EBITDA consensus above the $2m top of the guide. It is a weak edge because the beat pattern is visible to anyone, and the stock has not paid for beats.
evidence.independence: Q1 2026 beat figures from Barchart/StockStory (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/1753669/chegg-nysechgg-posts-better-than-expected-sales-in-q1-cy2026-but-stock-drops-11-6). The web-traffic finding below points the same way through a proxy.

evidence.text: Management guided Skilling (Busuu + Chegg Skills) to 'double-digit growth for the year' with a stronger second half (Q4 2025 release, 2026-02-09). H1 2026 Skilling was $35.1m ($17.6m Q1 +9%, $17.5m Q2 +2%) against $33.35m in H1 2025. A +10% full year ($76.5m) needs H2 Skilling of about $41.4m against $35.3m in H2 2025, i.e. +17%, while growth decelerated to +2% in Q2. Chegg also stopped giving segment guidance in Q2. The company's one stated growth engine is likely to show a visible miss against its own target, and the Q4 guide has come in below consensus three quarters running (Q2 guide $49.5m midpoint vs $58.6m consensus; Q3 guide $43.5m vs $48.3m; Q3 EBITDA $1.5m vs $6.0m).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: A next-quarter guide below consensus has gone with -14.56% (2026-08-06) and -10.67% (2026-02-09) close to close, and an intraday -11.6% on 2026-05-06 that closed +10.34%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The street focuses on total revenue now that segment guidance has gone, and no preview found mentions the Skilling target. If it were priced, previews would treat a reset of the Skilling target as expected, and Q4 consensus would sit below the seasonal run-rate (Q4/Q3 was 0.935 in 2025). Net of the rest of the company: Academic is about 60% of revenue, and the Q3 guide implies Academic about -57% y/y against -61% in Q2. A milder Academic decline in the Q4 guide could offset a Skilling disappointment, so the size is kept small.
evidence.independence: Q2 Skilling +2% from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm, a different document). The Coursera read-through below is a separate, independent proxy pointing the same way.

evidence.text: Chegg is out of compliance with the NYSE $1 minimum price again. The notice came 2026-07-24, the six-month cure runs to about 2027-01-24, and compliance needs a month-end close and 30-trading-day average of at least $1.00. Spot is $0.707, and stockholders approved a 1-for-4 to 1-for-15 reverse split on 2026-06-12 at the board's discretion. With roughly two month-ends left and the stock needing +41%, the board must act on the split within weeks, and an announcement alongside the Q3 release is plausible.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reverse split. The first deficiency (December 2025) was cured by the price on 2026-06-01, and the board then said it would not proceed with a split 'at this time' (Barchart, 2026-06-17).
evidence.why_not_priced: The notice is public but the timing is not. If the market had priced an imminent split, there would be pre-split selling by holders with sub-$1 or retail mandates; the stock has been flat (-1.8% over 20 days). It is probability-weighted: perhaps a one-in-three chance it lands inside the window.
evidence.independence: Annual meeting 8-K with the vote approving the 1:4 to 1:15 range (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000066/chgg-20260612.htm).

evidence.text: Third-party web traffic for Chegg (AltIndex, aggregated estimates) reads 3.32m visits in July, 3.26m in August and 4.93m in September 2026 (+51% m/m back-to-school). The Q3 average of 3.84m is down about 13% q/q from Q2's 4.40m (6.11m/3.94m/3.14m), against the roughly -24% q/q in Academic revenue implied by the Q3 guide ($43.5m less about $17.7m Skilling against Q2 Academic $34.3m).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same reported-quarter line as the first finding; beats have been sold (see above).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is an obscure aggregator series, and no preview cites it. It is a proxy only: a modelled estimate, with no year-ago September on the same provider (Semrush's October 2025 figure of 11.59m is a different model and not comparable), and subscription revenue lags traffic. If it were priced, consensus would sit above the guide midpoint.
evidence.independence: Shares direction with the first finding's beat pattern but rests on a different source. Proxy only.

evidence.text: Coursera, which reported after Chegg last spoke (2026-10-29), said Q3 consumer revenue fell 9% y/y on a normalized basis, that leading funnel indicators softened, and that it expects further consumer deceleration in Q4 and a low-double-digit consumer decline in 2027. This is a read-through to Chegg Skilling's consumer upskilling and language (Busuu) demand.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no direct history of Chegg reacting to peer prints; its guide line has been the mover (see the Skilling finding).
evidence.why_not_priced: It is a peer print after Chegg's last guide, so consensus may not have moved, and Chegg's Skilling estimates are thin (one analyst on Yahoo). It is a proxy: Coursera's consumer business is mostly courses and certificates, not language learning, so the transmission is unconfirmed.
evidence.independence: The consumer -9% figure comes from the MarketBeat call summary (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-coursera-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-29/). It points the same way as the Skilling finding but is a separate entity.

evidence.text: Chegg repaid the last $33.9m of its 0% convertible notes at maturity on 2026-09-01 and is debt-free, with about $38m of pro forma cash (June 30 cash of $72.3m less the repayment) against a market cap of about $78m. $120.7m remains on the buyback authorization, which was used for only $1.7m in Q2. With financing risk removed, a resumed or larger buyback, or a cash-floor narrative, is possible at the print.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to buyback news in the baseline window.
evidence.why_not_priced: The repayment is public, so this is mostly priced. What is not priced is any capital-return decision, and EV of about $40m against cash-burn risk (Q3 EBITDA guide $1-2m, capex about $3-4m a quarter) makes a large buyback less likely than a small one. The financing question was asked: the money retired debt, with no new financing, so it is neutral to slightly positive.
evidence.independence: Q2 release confirms the $120.7m authorization and $1.7m repurchased (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm).

evidence.text: Judge Mehta (D.D.C.) dismissed Chegg's antitrust suit against Google over AI Overviews on 2026-09-30. A litigation upside option that management had pointed to as a cause of the traffic collapse is gone, and the call may address an appeal or the costs.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline print was tied to this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public a month before the print and the stock barely moved. Only commentary on an appeal at the call is new.
evidence.independence: Same ruling reported by letsdatascience (https://letsdatascience.com/news/judge-dismisses-chegg-and-penske-ai-overviews-antitrust-laws-39a53d81); one fact, counted once.

evidence.text: On 2026-08-18 BARDA awarded Modification No. 21 to the CYFENDUS anthrax vaccine contract, worth about $24M, after the Aug 5 guide was set. The Sep 14 IR deck lists it as 'new in Q3'. If delivered in Q3 it is about 20% of the $110-130M Q3 revenue guide and could push revenue above the $123M consensus; the release gives no delivery quarter and does not say whether it was in guidance.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints driven by MCM contract timing have moved this stock hard both ways: Q2 2026 (accelerated MCM, with a guide cut) -29.6%; Q3 2025 +36.6%; Q2 2025 +36.7% (baseline history). The quarter's MCM revenue line has historically decided the sign together with the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue ($123.3M) sits above the guide midpoint ($120M) by only about $3M, which is less than this award. If the market were confident the award was incremental and in Q3, consensus would have moved toward or above the top of the range. No analyst note dated after the award was found, and coverage is thin (HC Wainwright the only named estimate).
evidence.independence: The Sep 14 2026 IR deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1367644/000136764426000091/hcw9-14x26ebs2026irconfe.htm) lists it as new in Q3, from the same issuer. The FY MCM guide is 'flat to slightly down', so it may already be inside guidance.

evidence.text: In Q3 Emergent repurchased $75M of its 3.875% 2028 unsecured notes for about $68M cash, roughly a 9% discount. Pro forma gross debt falls to $515M and cash to about $72M before Q3 operating cash flow. The result is a likely gain on extinguishment of about $7M plus about $2.9M a year of lower interest, all below operating income.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior: Q2 2026 carried a $20.5M loss on debt extinguishment from the OrbiMed term-loan refinancing, and the stock fell 29.6% on the guide cut, not on that line.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deck was filed as a 7.01 exhibit and no wire story was found on it. A consensus EPS of -$0.40 to -$0.45 likely excludes a gain on extinguishment. If it were priced, the GAAP EPS estimates would show it. On financing: the money buys down the 2028 maturity at a discount, which is deleveraging, not distress. The cost is that cash falls to about $72M on a name with $40M of annual interest.
evidence.independence: none; one document.

evidence.text: On 2026-08-31 the Government of Canada awarded Emergent a competitive standing offer to supply NARCAN Nasal Spray from 2026-10-01 to 2029-09-30, replacing the expiring five-year agreement. This retains an international naloxone channel that management could cite to firm the Commercial outlook (Q4 onward).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on this line is measurable; it is a renewal of an existing contract.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is public and a renewal, so it is largely inside expectations. It is only worth something if management uses it to hold the FY Commercial guide of -20% to -25%. A loss of the tender would have been a visible negative, and that did not happen.
evidence.independence: https://www.biopharmawatch.com/news/EBS/emergent-biosolutions-narcan-nasal-spray-canada (same announcement).

evidence.text: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter with Amphastar's Rextovy, a 4mg OTC naloxone approved 2026-06-16 and reportedly launched 2026-07-08, plus a 10mg prescription entrant launched in August. CDC provisional overdose deaths are down 12.3% year on year (12 months to March 2026), so Narcan volume and price could erode beyond the Aug 5 FY Commercial guide of -20% to -25%. Q2 naloxone was already $52.4M, down 22% year on year.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Naloxone erosion drove the Aug 5 2026 guide cut and the $191M NARCAN impairment: -29.6%. On Feb 26 2026 the FY2025 print with naloxone down 43% for the year moved -26.6%. This line has been sold hard each time it surprised negatively.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Aug 5 guide was cut explicitly for these entrants, and the Sep 14 deck names them. What is not priced is the size of the first full-quarter impact; no channel data (IQVIA/Circana) on Narcan share since July was found. If the market had priced a further cut, the stock would not be +5% over 5 days and +14.5% since the last print (EW post-earnings drift).
evidence.independence: This is a proxy, not a company number. The overdose-death trend comes from a different source: https://cdc.gov/overdose-prevention/data-research/facts-stats/index.html. Management's own Sep 14 deck says overdose deaths are falling faster than expected and pricing is more aggressive (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1367644/000136764426000091/hcw9-14x26ebs2026irconfe.htm). Net of the rest of the company: MCM (smallpox, anthrax, BAT) is the larger part of revenue and is contract-timed, so a naloxone miss can be offset by MCM deliveries.

evidence.text: The FY2026 guide (revenue $645-675M, adj. EBITDA $130-150M) against YTD revenue of $390.4M and YTD adj. EBITDA of $132M implies Q4 revenue of $125-175M, above the Q3 guide, and H2 adj. EBITDA of only $0-18M. The year therefore depends on Q4 MCM deliveries, and a reaffirmation is not a given on a name with eroding naloxone.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY guide has decided the last prints: a cut on Aug 5 2026 brought -29.6%; Q3 2025, when the guide was raised, brought +36.6% (baseline and the Aug 5 release).
evidence.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on public numbers, so the inputs are priced. The open question is the guide's direction on Nov 2, and the option market's 16.5% event move prices its size, not its sign.
evidence.independence: This shares a document with the bar and is an inference rather than a new fact. It is separate from the naloxone finding (its driver is the timing of MCM deliveries), but if the guide is cut, both findings land on that one line.

evidence.why_not_priced: Ichor has fallen about 40% since early October, while consensus still sits exactly on the guide midpoint ($330.2m) and the whisper equals consensus. If the market had priced a customer growing 22% q/q into Ichor's quarter, the whisper would sit above consensus and the stock would not be near its post-earnings low. Ichor has not spoken since Aug 3, so Lam's print is newer than the guide.
evidence.independence: UCT, a peer selling to the same two customers, beat the top of its Q3 guide (+18% q/q, next finding; different document). Applied Materials guided semi-systems +12% q/q for Aug-Oct (https://247wallst.com/cards/applied-materials-q3-2026-earnings-amat-01kzybvthd5qqamwrtqk59k25x). Lam's customer share comes from Ichor 10-Ks (e.g. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652535/000156459022007613/ichr-10k_20211231.htm). This is a proxy: a subsystem supplier's revenue does not track Lam's quarter one for one.

evidence.text: Ultra Clean (UCT), Ichor's closest listed peer with the same two dominant customers, reported Q3 2026 on Oct 27. Revenue was a record $759.0m, +18% q/q, above the top of its $700-750m guide, and it guided Q4 to $800-860m (+9% q/q at the midpoint). That points to both an Ichor Q3 revenue beat and a Q4 guide able to reach the ~$355m implied bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ichor's guidance line has moved the stock the most: +32.7% on the Feb 2026 raised outlook and -11.2% on Q2 2026, when margins and the ramp disappointed. UCT itself traded at $51.48 on Oct 27 and $49.71 (-9.12%) on Oct 30 (https://www.trivano.com/persbericht/770834-770834.html), so the peer's beat-and-raise was not held by the market.
evidence.why_not_priced: Ichor traded around $38 on Oct 26 (Earnings Whispers), rose to $43.08 by Oct 29 and gave it back to about $38.30 today, so the peer read-through was briefly priced and then erased in sector selling. Consensus Q3 has not moved off the guide midpoint since UCT reported.
evidence.independence: Lam's +22% q/q (previous finding, separate document). Lam's commentary on 2027 WFE and on supply constraints (next findings) shares one Lam document with the first finding but makes a different claim. Caveat: UCT's inventory rose to $723m from $391m in December 2025, so part of its growth is stocking; that applies to Ichor too (its Q2 inventory build was $38.4m).

evidence.text: On Oct 21 Lam put preliminary 2027 WFE at more than $200bn, against a mid-$150bn 2026 (about +30%), and expects about 10 new Tier-1 fabs in 2027. That supports Ichor's August statement that customer visibility extends 'well into 2027'. The stock has derated on doubts about exactly that multi-quarter ramp.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Feb 2026: a raised forward outlook took the stock +32.7%. Since then forward commentary has been sold (Aug -11.2%).
evidence.why_not_priced: Lam's own stock fell 11.8% on that same call (https://www.allinvestview.com/earnings/LRCX/q1-2027/), and Citi said on Oct 23 that the semicap selloff 'could be just the beginning'. The market is pricing AI-capex doubt, not the customer's 2027 number. If the 2027 outlook were priced, Ichor would not trade at 66% below its high with 10.5% bullish sentiment.
evidence.independence: Ichor's own Q2 release says customer visibility reaches 'well into 2027' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001652535/000165253526000066/ex-991_26q2xearnings.htm). This finding shares the Lam call with the supply-constraint finding below, which makes a different claim.

evidence.text: Lam guided its December quarter to only $8.6bn (+4.6% q/q) and said it would have been higher without component supply and clean-room constraints, with China revenue 'significantly lower'. Ichor needs about $355m in Q4 (+8% q/q off $330m) to meet its own FY >=30% commitment, and it flagged a late-Q2 parts shortage from a flow-control supplier. Both put the Q4 guide and margins at risk.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: margins and the ramp disappointed and the stock fell 11.2%. 2025: guide-related misses gave -31.4% (Nov 2025), -30.2% (Aug 2025) and -23.2% (May 2025), all in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Earnings Whispers names the flow-control supplier as the 'obvious risk' (https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/ICHR/21402). But consensus has not moved and nobody has tied Lam's +4.6% December quarter to Ichor's ~$355m implied Q4. Subsystem shipments lead tool revenue, so Lam's slower December quarter could show up in Ichor's Q4 guide.
evidence.independence: Earnings Whispers on Ichor's flow-control supplier and its Q2 slip (separate source). UCT's +9% q/q Q4 guide (above) cuts against this finding, so it is sized net of that. This finding shares the Lam call with the 2027 WFE finding above.

evidence.text: Applied Materials, Ichor's second-largest customer (~25-35% of sales in past 10-Ks), guided FQ4 2026 (Aug-Oct) semiconductor-systems revenue to about $7.9bn, +12% q/q from $7.04bn, in line with Ichor's guided +12% midpoint.

evidence.text: October's semicap tape is a reaction function that sells beats.
